test_title: PYST 23: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - English (Held On: 19th Sep 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct Indirect Speech form:

She said, “I like reading novels.”

options.text: She said that she likes reading novels.
She said that she liked reading novels.
She said she was liking novels.
She said she had liked novels.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she liked reading novels.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"I like" becomes "she liked"**
 
 
• The pronoun "I" is changed to "she" to match the subject in indirect speech.
 
• Verb "like" is changed to "liked" to reflect the past tense in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Quotation removal:**
 
 
• The direct speech is converted into a reported statement without quotation marks.
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is transformed into an indirect clause introduced by "that."
 
• The sentence structure in indirect speech is modified to reflect past tense consistency.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said that she liked reading novels."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said that she likes reading novels."
 
 
• The verb "likes" is in the present tense, which is incorrect in this context as it violates the rule of tense backshifting in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She said she was liking novels."
 
 
• The use of "was liking" is grammatically incorrect as "like" is a stative verb and does not typically appear in progressive forms.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said she had liked novels."
 
 
• The use of "had liked" implies a completed action in the past, which changes the original meaning of the statement.
 
 
</ul
